label: Sequences & Series
overview: SAT questions on sequences focus on arithmetic sequences (constant difference between terms) and geometric sequences (constant ratio between terms). You need to find a specific term, find the common difference or ratio, or sum a finite geometric series. Recognising which type of sequence you have is the first step.

workedExamples.problem: An arithmetic sequence has first term 7 and common difference 4. What is the 15th term?

commonMistakes.mistake: Using n instead of (n−1) in the nth term formula: a₁ + nd
commonMistakes.fix: The first term already counts as position 1, so you only add (n−1) steps of d to reach position n.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing arithmetic and geometric — applying the wrong formula
commonMistakes.fix: Check: does each term differ by the same amount (arithmetic) or multiply by the same ratio (geometric)? Compute two consecutive differences or ratios to confirm.

quickTip: For arithmetic sequences subtract consecutive terms to find d. For geometric divide. Once you know the type and the first two values, every other term is mechanical.
